Knowledge and behavioral changes among men who have sex with men (MSM) are evaluated through the collection and analysis of data from HIV and STI testing registers, bi-annual cohort surveys of MSM, and case reports from infectious disease clinics for individuals referred to confirmatory testing at CheckpointLX. 2. Between 2011 and February 2015, a total of 8,311 rapid HIV tests were conducted. Among these, 3% of tests in women and men who have sex with women were reactive. Additionally, 243 MSM with reactive test results were referred to NHS facilities for confirmatory testing. 3. For MSM referred to NHS facilities and confirmed as HIV-positive, clinical data were available for 127 cases. The median CD4 count was 498 cells/mm³, and the median viral load was 270,009 copies/mm³. Nearly all (98%) of these individuals initiated antiretroviral therapy immediately. 4. All reactive HIV tests were referred for confirmatory testing, and individuals with confirmed positive results were linked to treatment through the NHS. Client satisfaction surveys conducted in 2012 and 2014 revealed high levels of satisfaction with CheckpointLX facilities, including reception support, waiting times, and the quality of information provided. 5. In 2012, the Association of HIV-Affected Women and Their Families (Demetra) launched a mobile HIV testing services (HTS) summer tour to increase access to testing for all population groups, with a focus on key populations such as MSM, people who inject drugs (PWID), sex workers, the homeless, and individuals in or recently released from prison. 6. The mobile HTS services were provided in convenient and acceptable settings for the target populations. In addition to testing, Demetra engaged in advocacy by meeting with policymakers, public health authorities, and media representatives. The program has been repeated annually since 2012, covering 14 cities in Lithuania, with some cities receiving repeat visits. 7. Demetra adheres to national guidelines and AIDS Healthcare Foundation principles to ensure linkage to care and treatment for all individuals diagnosed with HIV. The organization employs a health coordinator for medical purposes and a social coordinator for client counseling. Over 80 media communications have been disseminated since 2012 to promote the program. 8. From 2012 to 2014, Demetra provided 2,644 rapid HIV tests and counseling sessions, with 86% of clients being first-time testers. Among these, 25% belonged to key populations. Eleven clients had reactive results, were referred for confirmatory testing, and were diagnosed as HIV-positive. No false positives were reported. 9. Demetra also distributed 39,000 condoms with accurate HIV prevention information. Advocacy efforts motivated five healthcare providers to join the HIV testing network and commit to future outreach collaboration. 10. The Catalan Health Department initiated the DEVO Project in 1994 to complement facility-based HIV testing by funding community-based organizations to provide free, voluntary, and confidential HTS. The network now includes 12 HTS sites, primarily operated by NGOs, serving diverse populations, including MSM, PWID, sex workers, and young people aged 15–24. 11. Peer counselors in the DEVO Project are trained to collect blood samples and perform rapid tests for HIV and syphilis. The project also provides HIV prevention services and uses a web-based data entry tool for systematic data analysis in collaboration with the Center for Epidemiological Studies on HIV/STI of Catalonia (CEEISCAT). 12. From 1995 to 2006, the number of HIV tests performed annually in Catalonia increased from 716 to 1,849. Despite this increase, the overall positivity rate remained constant. The DEVO Project currently diagnoses 20% of all HIV cases reported in Catalonia, demonstrating the strategic success of targeted HTS programs. 13. In 2007, outreach HTS programs were established in Macedonia as part of the Global Fund initiative. The Health Education and Research Association (HERA) organized mobile units to provide HTS in 11 cities and 10 rural areas, targeting key populations such as sex workers, MSM, PWID, and prisoners. 14. HERA employs health professionals and peer counselors from key populations to provide community-based HTS. Services include rapid HIV testing, preand post-test counseling, referrals for confirmatory testing, and linkage to care for those diagnosed as HIV-positive. 15. From 2007 to 2014, HERA provided HTS to 13,071 clients, 85% of whom belonged to key populations. Thirty-three clients with reactive results were confirmed as HIV-positive. The program successfully reintegrated 36 individuals into care and linked all HIV-positive MSM to treatment. 16. In Kyrgyzstan, rapid HIV testing was piloted in 2012 through NGOs, following a Ministry of Health order. Twelve NGOs were authorized to conduct oral fluid-based rapid HIV testing, with quality control guidelines in place. The program targeted key populations, including MSM, PWID, and sex workers. 17. During the first year, 4,500 clients received HIV testing, with 226 reactive results referred for confirmatory testing. Ultimately, 22 new HIV-positive diagnoses were made, and 36 previously undiagnosed individuals were reintegrated into care. 18. The IN-Mouraria project in Lisbon, launched in 2012, provides harm reduction interventions and HTS for PWID and migrant populations. Services are free, confidential, and accessible without appointments or identification. The project operates in a high-risk urban area and collaborates with local organizations. 19. Between 2012 and 2014, IN-Mouraria provided HTS to 845 clients, including migrants (52%), the general population (29%), PWID (11%), and other key populations (8%). Active referrals to care were offered to all newly or previously diagnosed HIV-positive clients. 20. The DETECT-HIV project in Milan, initiated in 2013, focused on providing HTS to high-risk populations, including MSM, PWID, and migrants. Rapid HIV testing was conducted in various settings, and clients with reactive results were referred for confirmatory testing and care. 21. From 2013 to 2014, DETECT-HIV performed 399 rapid tests, with seven reactive results. Five clients were confirmed as HIV-positive, and three were linked to care. Over one-third of clients had never been tested for HIV before, citing the convenience of non-facility-based testing as a motivating factor.
